day-1.t: Day 1 — Find the words your customer actually types

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write down 10 real searches a customer would type
Stop using the words you use inside the shop
Choose one main keyword for your home page

b.v: About 20 minutes. You need a notebook, a pen and your phone. No computer needed.

Most small business websites fail at the first step. The owner writes for himself: 'Quality steel fabrication solutions since 2011'. The customer types 'iron gate Lahore'. SEO starts by learning the customer's words, not by learning a trick.
1) Collect the real words
Ask five people who are not in your business what they would type if they needed you today. Their answers are worth more than any tool.

Do this in your notebook:|Write your business in one plain line: 'I make and fit iron gates in Lahore'|Now write five ways a customer might search it|Write the city or area next to each one|Ask two past customers what they typed before they found you (a WhatsApp message is enough)
2) Check which words Google already expects
Google's own search box is a free keyword tool. Type your word slowly and read the suggestions that appear under it.

v: Autocomplete = the list of suggestions Google shows under the search box. It comes from what people really type.
People also ask = the question box in results. Each line is a topic you could write about.
Related searches = the suggestions at the bottom of page one.

b.v: Spend 10 minutes:|Type 'iron gate' and read every suggestion|Note any that mention your city|Scroll to the bottom of the results page and copy the related searches|Write the ones that fit your work into the notebook
3) Pick one main keyword per page
A keyword is simply the phrase you want a page to be found for. One page gets one main keyword. If you chase five phrases on one page, Google cannot tell what the page is about.
Example: the home page of a Lahore gate maker targets 'iron gate Lahore'. A second page about fixing broken gates targets 'gate repair Lahore'. Two pages, two jobs, no fighting.

The most common beginner mistake is choosing a phrase nobody types, like 'best premium quality steel fabrication solutions in Pakistan'. Long, fancy and empty. Write the way a tired customer types at 11 pm on a phone.
Practice

Do it now, before the next lesson:|Open a new note called Keywords|List 10 searches, each with your city or area|Mark the one you think is most likely to bring a paying customer|Send me (or yourself) that list on WhatsApp so it is saved

day-2.t: Day 2 — Set up the free tools that tell you the truth

b.v: Today's goal

v: Create a Google account you control, not one your cousin controls
Connect your site to Google Search Console
See the searches your site already appears for

b.v: About 25 minutes. Do this on a computer or laptop if you can. The menus are wide.

Search Console is Google's free report card for your website. It shows the searches you appear in, the pages Google has stored, and any errors. Without it you are guessing. It costs nothing and takes one evening.
1) Fix who owns the accounts
Many small businesses lose their website because the developer owns the Google account. Use a business email you control, with a password your family can find if something happens to you.

Set up clean ownership:|Create or use a Gmail such as yourshopname@gmail.com|Turn on two-step verification|Write the password in a diary at home, not only in your phone|Add one trusted family member as a recovery contact
2) Add your site to Search Console
You will prove the site is yours. The easiest proof for beginners is a small text record added in your domain settings, or the HTML file your developer can drop on the server.

Do this:|Go to search.google.com/search-console|Choose 'Domain' and type your domain without www|Google gives you a TXT record to copy|Send it to your hosting or domain company and ask them to add it|Come back and press Verify|Wait a day, then open 'Performance'
3) Read the two numbers that matter first

In Performance you will see Impressions and Clicks. Impressions are times your site appeared in results. Clicks are times someone chose it. A page with many impressions and few clicks has a title problem, which you will fix on Day 3.

v: Impressions = how often your page was shown in search results
Clicks = how often someone actually opened it
Average position = roughly where you appeared. 1 is the top.
Queries = the exact words people used

b.v: Do not panic in week one. A new site can show almost nothing for weeks. Search Console is a slow diary, not a light switch. Check it weekly, not hourly.
Practice
Do this today:|Verify your site in Search Console|Open Performance and set the date range to the last 3 months|Screenshot the top five queries|Write one sentence: what is my site already known for?

day-3.t: Day 3 — On-page basics: titles, headings and honest text

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write a page title a human wants to click
Use one clear heading per page
Put the keyword in the text without stuffing it

b.v: About 20 minutes. You will edit one page only today. One page done properly beats ten pages half done.
On-page SEO means the things on the page itself: the title, the headings, the words, the links. It is the part you fully control, and it is where most small sites lose easy clicks.
1) The page title is your shop sign in the results
The title tag is the blue line in Google results. It is not always the same as the big heading on your page. Keep it around 60 characters so phones do not cut it off.
Notice the order: what it is, where, then the shop name. Notice the description gives a reason to click: free measurement, ten days, fitting included.
2) One H1, then real sub-headings
The H1 is the main heading of the page. Use one. Then use H2 for each section. This helps a reader skim on a phone and helps Google understand the order of your ideas.

v: H1 = main heading, once per page, close to your main keyword
H2 = section heading for each big idea
Alt text = the short description you give an image, read aloud by screen readers

b.v: 3) Write like a helpful shopkeeper

Write 300 to 600 plain words on a service page: what you do, who it is for, sizes and materials, price range, areas you cover, how long it takes, how to contact you. Then stop. Long thin pages full of repeated keywords do not rank and do not sell.

Keyword stuffing is the classic mistake: 'iron gate Lahore, iron gate price Lahore, best iron gate Lahore' in every line. Google reads it as spam and customers close the tab. Use the phrase where it fits naturally, maybe three or four times on a page, and use plain alternatives elsewhere.
Practice

Fix one page now:|Open your most important service page|Rewrite the title as: service + city + shop name|Check there is one H1 and it mentions the service|Add a price range and the areas you cover|Add one clear way to contact you above the fold, meaning before the reader scrolls

day-4.t: Day 4 — Google Business Profile: your free shop window

b.v: Today's goal

v: Claim or create your Business Profile
Fill every field that affects local searches
Add photos and a working WhatsApp button

b.v: About 25 minutes. This is the single highest-value free action for a shop or clinic with a physical address.

When someone in Rawalpindi searches 'tailor near me', Google shows a map with three businesses. That map is fed by Google Business Profile, a free listing. A complete profile can bring phone calls in days, while a new website takes months.
1) Claim the listing properly
Search your business name on Google Maps. If a listing already exists, claim it. If not, create it. Google will verify you, usually by postcard, phone or a short video of your premises.

Do this:|Search your shop name plus city on Google Maps|If it exists, press 'Claim this business'. If not, press 'Add a missing place'|Choose the most specific category you can, such as 'Tailor' not 'Clothing store'|Enter the exact address and a phone number you answer|Complete verification when Google asks
2) Fill the fields that decide who sees you
Google matches a search to your categories, your service list, your area and your name. Vague profiles disappear.

v: Primary category = the one job you most want. It matters more than all the extras.
Services = add each service with a short plain line, such as 'School uniform stitching, 3 days'
Service area = the areas you really travel to, not the whole province
Hours = real hours, and update them before Eid holidays
Attributes = things like 'On-site services' or 'Wheelchair accessible'

b.v: 3) Photos and a WhatsApp button
Profiles with real photos get far more calls than empty ones. Use daylight, clean the counter, and show the work, not only the signboard.

Add today:|Three photos of finished work|One photo of the shop front so people recognise it|One photo of you or your team, if you are comfortable|Paste your WhatsApp link in the website field so the chat button works

Do not put keywords in your business name, like 'Ali Tailors Best Cheap Stitching Rawalpindi'. Google suspends profiles for that, and a suspended profile can vanish from the map overnight. Your name is your name.
Practice
Finish this before Day 5:|Complete every empty field in your profile|Upload four photos|Write your services with prices or price ranges|Ask one happy customer to leave a review this week

day-5.t: Day 5 — Local SEO: reviews, maps and being consistent

b.v: Today's goal

v: Get reviews the honest way
Keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere
Write short local pages that mention real areas

b.v: About 20 minutes. Reviews are the strongest local signal you can influence without paying.

Local SEO means being found by people near you. Three things decide it: how complete your profile is, how many genuine reviews you have, and whether the internet agrees about your address and phone number.
1) Ask for reviews at the right moment
The best moment is right after you hand over the work and the customer is happy. Ask in person, then send the link on WhatsApp the same day. Keep it short and never offer money for a review.

The review routine:|In your Business Profile, press 'Ask for reviews' and copy the link|Save that link in your WhatsApp quick replies|After every job, send: 'Thank you. If you have 30 seconds, a short review helps our small shop a lot: [link]'|Reply to every review within two days, good or bad
2) Say the same thing everywhere
Google compares your details with other sites. If your phone number is different on Facebook, your listing looks unreliable. This is called NAP consistency: Name, Address, Phone.

v: NAP = Name, Address, Phone. Keep them word for word the same.
Citation = any mention of your business details on another site, such as a directory
Pick one phone number and use it everywhere, even if you have three

b.v: Check and fix:|Search your shop name in Google and look at the results|Open your Facebook page and your listing side by side|Make the address text identical, including the shop number|Fix anything that is old, such as a closed second branch
3) Write pages for the areas you really serve

A page for each area works when the content is genuinely different: delivery time, fitting charges, the roads you cover, a job you did there. Five copied pages with the area name swapped is a penalty waiting to happen.
Example: a Sialkot sports goods seller writes one page for 'custom cricket bats Sialkot' and one for 'club kit bulk orders Sialkot'. Different buyers, different questions, different prices.
Fake reviews are easy to buy and easy to detect. Google removes them and can suspend the profile. A shop with eight real reviews and one honest reply to a bad review beats fifty bought stars.
Practice

Do this now:|Send the review link to two past customers|Reply to your newest review, even if it is old|Fix any phone number that differs between your listing and your Facebook page|Write down the three areas you truly serve in one week

day-6.t: Day 6 — Speed and mobile: why your site loses customers

b.v: Today's goal

v: Find out how slow your site is on a phone
Fix the two or three things that cause most of the delay
Make the phone version usable with one thumb

b.v: About 20 minutes. You do not need to be a developer, but you may need to send two messages to one.
Most visitors in Pakistan arrive on a phone, often on mobile data. If a page takes long to show, they leave before they see your price. Speed is not a technical luxury; it is lost sales.
1) Measure it the free way
PageSpeed Insights is a free Google tool. It gives a score for phone and for desktop, plus a list of problems in plain words.

Do this:|Open pagespeed.web.dev on your laptop|Enter your home page and run the test|Switch to the Mobile tab and note the score|Scroll to 'Opportunities' and read the top three items|Screenshot the list and send it to your developer
2) The usual culprits
In small business sites the same few problems repeat. Fixing them is often enough.

v: Huge images = a 4 MB photo from a phone camera shrunk to 1200 pixels wide and saved as .webp
Too many plugins = remove anything you do not use, especially sliders
Cheap shared hosting = if the server is slow, nothing on the page can be fast
Render-blocking scripts = ask your developer to load chat widgets and fonts later

b.v: 3) Design for one thumb
Open your own site on your phone and try to buy or call. If you have to pinch or zoom, a customer will not bother.

The phone test:|Can you read the first screen without zooming?|Is the phone number or WhatsApp button visible without scrolling?|Are buttons big enough for a thumb?|Does the enquiry form ask for more than name and number?

Do not chase a perfect score. A 100 score with no clear price and no contact button sells nothing. Aim for a page that opens quickly and answers 'what do you sell and how much' in the first screen. Scores move for reasons outside your control, so treat them as a hint, not a target.
Practice

Do this now:|Run the phone test on your own site|Shrink your three biggest photos and upload them again|Add a WhatsApp button to the top of the home page|Ask one person over 50 to find your price on their phone and watch where they get stuck

day-7.t: Day 7 — A content plan you can actually keep

b.v: Today's goal

v: List 12 questions customers ask before buying
Turn them into a simple 12-week plan
Write one page in 40 minutes with a repeatable shape

b.v: About 25 minutes. This is the lesson that keeps working for a year.
Content is not blogging for its own sake. Every page should answer a question a paying customer asks. If you cannot name the customer who would read it, do not write it.
1) Collect the questions you already answer daily
Your WhatsApp inbox is a keyword research tool. Every repeated question is a page you are missing.
Do this:|Scroll your WhatsApp for one week of customer chats|Copy every question into a note|Group them: price, timing, quality, delivery, after-sales|Keep the ones asked more than twice
2) Build a 12-week plan
One page a week is enough. Twelve good pages in a year will beat a burst of twenty thin pages in one month that you never update.

v: Week 1 to 4 = the price and process questions. These bring buyers closest to paying.
Week 5 to 8 = comparisons, such as 'iron gate or steel gate'
Week 9 to 12 = local and seasonal, such as 'gate repair before monsoon in Karachi'
Keep one page per question. Update it when your prices change.

b.v: 3) A page shape that works every time
Use the same six parts so writing gets faster and readers always find the price.

Write in this order:|The question as the H1, in the customer's words|A two-line answer, including the price range|What affects the price, as a short list|One real example with a rupee figure|What to do next, with your phone number|Three common mistakes customers make

Example opening for a Karachi AC repair page: 'AC service in Karachi usually costs between Rs 2,500 and Rs 6,000 depending on the unit size and whether gas needs refilling. Here is how to tell which one you need.' That answers in two lines and earns the scroll.

Do not publish pages written by copying a competitor and swapping the city. It reads badly, it competes with the original, and it gives the customer no reason to call you. Your own job photos and your own price ranges are the difference.
Practice

Do this now:|Write your list of 12 questions|Pick the one asked most often|Draft that page today using the six parts above, even roughly|Send the draft to one customer and ask: does this answer your question?

day-8.t: Day 8 — Links and reputation, without buying them

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand what a backlink is and why it counts
Find five realistic places to be listed
Avoid the traps that get sites punished

b.v: About 20 minutes. Expect slow results. Links are the slowest part of SEO and the easiest to ruin.

A backlink is a link from another website to yours. Google treats it as a vote of confidence. One link from a real local newspaper or a supplier directory is worth more than a hundred links from a link farm.
1) Links a small business can honestly earn
You do not need a marketing agency to get your first ten links. You need to be listed where your customers already look.

v: Local directories = your city's business listings and trade associations
Suppliers and partners = 'where to buy' pages of brands you stock
Chambers and markets = chamber of commerce or market association member lists
Local press = a real story, such as training three women to stitch, not a press release about a sale
Your own profiles = Facebook, Instagram and YouTube, filled in properly

b.v: Start with five:|List the five places your customers already trust|Check whether each has a website with a members or sellers page|Email or WhatsApp a short request with your name, one line about the shop and your link|Do one per week, not all five today
2) What a good link looks like
Ask three questions. Is the site real? Does it serve people like your customers? Would you be comfortable showing the link to a customer? If any answer is no, skip it.
3) The traps
People selling '500 backlinks for Rs 3,000' are selling links Google ignores or penalises. The risk is not only wasted money; a penalty can remove your pages from results for months.

Never pay for links disguised as reviews, never join a link exchange group with strangers, and never let an agency add hidden links or hidden text to your site. If an offer sounds like a guaranteed number one ranking, it is a lie: nobody can guarantee Google's ranking.
Practice

Do this now:|Write the five realistic places from step 1|Send the first request today, by email or WhatsApp|Add the link to a simple sheet: site, date asked, date live|Check your Facebook and Instagram bios actually link to your site

day-9.t: Day 9 — Measure what matters, ignore the rest

b.v: Today's goal

v: Read four numbers in Search Console without confusion
Know the difference between a visit and an enquiry
Build a one-page monthly report for yourself

b.v: About 20 minutes. If you sell through WhatsApp, you must count WhatsApp taps, not only form fills.
SEO is not a score. It is a set of small changes in how many right people find you and contact you. Without measurement you keep paying for work you cannot judge.
1) The four numbers to watch
Open Search Console once a week, same day, same time. Look at the trend, not one day.

v: Clicks = people arriving from Google search
Impressions = times you were shown. Rising impressions with flat clicks means your titles need work.
Queries on page 2 = words where you appear around position 11 to 20. These are the easiest wins.
Top pages = which pages actually earn the visits

b.v: 2) Count enquiries, not traffic
A thousand visits with no calls is a hobby. Install a free analytics tool, or simpler, use a WhatsApp click link so you can see how many people pressed it.

Set up basic counting:|Use a wa.me link on your buttons instead of a plain number|Add the page name to the message so you know where the chat started|Keep a paper log: date, name, area, what they asked|Once a month, write the number of real enquiries next to the traffic number
3) A one-page monthly report
You do not need a dashboard. Five lines in a notebook forces you to notice what changed.
Every first Sunday of the month, write:|Clicks this month, and last month|My three best queries|Enquiries from the website|What I changed last month|One thing I will change this month

Do not judge a change after three days. Google needs weeks to re-crawl and re-rank, and normal results move up and down. Change one thing, wait a month, then judge. Changing five things at once teaches you nothing.
Practice

Do this now:|Open Search Console and sort queries by position|Find every query sitting between position 11 and 20|Pick the one closest to your money service|Improve that page's title and first paragraph today

day-10.t: Day 10 — The mistakes that waste a year, and your 30-day plan

b.v: Today's goal

v: Recognise the six mistakes that sink small business SEO
Put your next 30 days on one page
Know when to stop doing SEO yourself

b.v: About 25 minutes. Then keep the plan where you can see it.
Most small businesses do not fail at SEO because Google is unfair. They fail because they chase tricks, change direction every month, and never finish anything. Finishing is the strategy.
1) The six mistakes

v: Targeting words nobody types, such as 'world class solutions'
One page trying to sell everything, so it ranks for nothing
No prices and no phone number on the first screen
A slow, broken phone version that eats the traffic you earned
Buying links or reviews, then losing the listing
Changing the plan every three weeks and finishing nothing

b.v: 2) Your 30-day plan
This uses everything from the course. It fits around a full working day if you give it 30 minutes, four evenings a week.

Week 1:|Finish the Business Profile completely and add four photos|Verify Search Console|Fix the title and H1 of your main service page|Week 2:|Add prices or price ranges to your top three pages|Compress images and add a WhatsApp button|Ask five customers for reviews|Week 3:|Write two question pages from your list of twelve|Fix your NAP details across Facebook and your listing|Week 4:|Ask for two local directory listings|Set up the WhatsApp click link|Write your first monthly report
3) When to pay for help

Do the free work yourself first. Then pay for help only with clear deliverables: a written list of pages, a monthly report you can read, and no promises of exact rankings. Ask for the report before you pay, and check that the work actually exists on your site.

Be careful with anyone who asks for admin access to your domain or your Google account, or who wants to put their own name on your listing. Give editing rights only where needed, and keep ownership in your hands. If you part ways, you must still control your site and profile.
Practice

Finish the course with this:|Copy the 30-day plan into your phone's calendar as 16 short events|Do the first task today, not Monday|Write the one number you want higher in 90 days, such as enquiries per month|Check that number on the first Sunday of next month
